item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
Mostly negative. 2024 shows some anti-corruption capacity still operating, but the strongest evidence points to persistent patronage, dynastic advantage, weak KPK independence, and business-state privilege rather than a ruler systematically resisting capture.

**Accepted Claims**

- **Corruption Perceptions Index 2024: Indonesia** — Transparency International, 2025-02-11, https://www.transparency.org/en/cpi/2024/index/idn  
  Indonesia’s CPI score rose to 37/100, up 3 points from 2023, which is weak positive evidence that corruption pressure did not worsen across the year. The same page still shows corruption as severe, so this is only a limited positive signal.  
  IDs: `5B.5`

- **OECD Economic Surveys: Indonesia 2024** — OECD, 2024-11-26, https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-indonesia-2024_de87555a-en/full-report/accelerating-growth-and-attaining-socioeconomic-convergence_02e70f46.html  
  OECD says fighting corruption remained a long-running priority and notes the KPK investigated 281 cases and prosecuted more than 200 corruption cases from Jan 2022 to Dec 2023. That is positive evidence that anti-graft institutions were still functioning.  
  IDs: `5B.5`, also `5B.4`

- **Accelerating growth and attaining socioeconomic convergence: OECD Economic Surveys: Indonesia 2024** — OECD, 2024-11-26, https://www.oecd-ilibrary.org/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-indonesia-2024_de87555a-en.html  
  The same survey says Indonesia remained relatively restrictive, with widespread state involvement, weak lobbying rules, and SOE governance not aligned with best practice. That supports a negative finding on resisting monopoly and oligarchic capture.  
  IDs: `5B.5`, also `5B.4`

- **Current challenges and strategic directions for land administration system modernisation in Indonesia** — Taylor & Francis, 2024-06-06, https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/14498596.2024.2360531  
  The article says land administration still had regulatory gaps, inefficient registration, validation issues, and resource constraints. That is negative evidence on resisting favoritism in property/land allocation and on clean property-rights administration.  
  IDs: `5B.5`, also `5B.4`

- **World Bank Group Debars PT. LPPSLH Konsultan** — World Bank, 2024-07-10, https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/10/world-bank-group-debars-pt-lppslh-konsultan  
  The World Bank said the firm overbilled an Indonesia project and improperly hired a project official’s family member. This is concrete negative evidence that favoritism and corrupt procurement practices persisted inside state-linked development work.  
  IDs: `5B.5`, also `5B.4`

- **Indonesia’s CPI 2024 page** — Transparency International, 2025-02-11, https://www.transparency.org/en/countries/indonesia/  
  Transparency International says 92% of people think government corruption is a big problem and that 30% of public-service users paid a bribe in the prior 12 months. This is strong negative background evidence against effective resistance to corruption.  
  IDs: `5B.5`

- **Reuters: Jokowi seeks Golkar takeover to retain decade-long influence** — The Jakarta Post / Reuters, 2024-03-20, https://www.thejakartapost.com/indonesia/2024/03/20/jokowi-seeks-golkar-takeover-to-retain-decade-long-influence  
  Reuters reported Jokowi was trying to install a loyal ally to lead Golkar and secure a post-office role, framed as preserving influence and family interests. That is negative evidence for resisting oligarchic and patronage politics.  
  IDs: `5B.5`, also `4B.8`, `5B.2`

- **Reuters: Protests across Indonesia as parliament delays change to election law** — Reuters via ThePrint, 2024-08-22, https://theprint.in/world/protests-across-indonesia-as-parliament-delays-change-to-election-law/2233305/  
  Reuters said planned election-law changes would have benefited Jokowi’s youngest son and were widely seen as nepotism and power consolidation. That is direct negative evidence for favoritism and politically connected advantage.  
  IDs: `5B.5`, also `4B.8`

- **Analysis: A decade of Jokowi, Indonesia’s democracy icon, leaves illiberal legacy, critics say** — Reuters via ThePrint, 2024-10-14, https://theprint.in/world/analysis-a-decade-of-jokowi-indonesias-democracy-icon-leaves-illiberal-legacy-critics-say/2310394/  
  Reuters’ end-of-term analysis says Jokowi left patronage, dynastic politics, and weaker institutional integrity. This is broad but important negative evidence against a clean anti-corruption or anti-oligarchy record.  
  IDs: `5B.5`, also `4B.10`, `5B.2`

- **Jokowi effect: how Indonesia’s outgoing leader shaped election to succeed him** — Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-02-12, https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/jokowi-effect-how-indonesias-outgoing-leader-shaped-election-to-succeed-him-3300317  
  Reuters said Jokowi’s son joining Prabowo’s ticket created a perceived incumbent seal of approval and shifted coalition behavior. This is indirect negative evidence for resisting politically connected business and elite privileges.  
  IDs: `5B.5`, also `4B.8`

- **Indonesia Growth and Jobs Report: Running Faster, for Longer** — World Bank, 2024, https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/indonesia/publication/indonesia-growth-and-jobs-report-running-faster-for-longer-structural-transformation-productivity-and-good-jobs  
  The report diagnoses market power, regulatory barriers, and non-tariff/services restrictions as drag factors. That is negative evidence that the business environment still allowed monopoly-like distortions and privileged incumbency.  
  IDs: `5B.5`, also `5B.4`

**Search Gap**  
Direct evidence that Jokowi personally launched a major anti-corruption or anti-oligarchy crackdown in 2024 was sparse. The strongest positive evidence is institutional and aggregate, not clearly presidential: a slightly better CPI score and continued KPK casework. The dominant pattern in the sources is still patronage, dynastic advantage, and structural capture.
